physical_harm: Severe injuries including unconsciousness and potential death
number_of_offences: Multiple offences/counts charged, some finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the statement of the appellant, who was the injured eye witness, and specifically named the private respondents in the FIR as key evidence.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly the appellant, as credible and noted that he stood the test of cross-examination and was bound to state what was in the FIR, otherwise he would be accused of contradictions.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 27.07.2016; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: 28.08.2020; Supreme Court decision: 15.03.2021
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: R. Basant, Atul Kumar, Abhimanyu Sharma, Ms. Deepali, Pulak Bagchi, Tarun Gupta; Counsel for the State: Anil Kaushik, AAG, Haryana, Vivek Sood, Sr. Adv., Sanjay Kumar Visen, Sanjeev Prakash Upadhyaya, Shashi Pratap Singh, Ms. Monisha Handa, Mohit D. Ram
investigation_status: FIR registered (477 of 2016), charge-sheet filed against other accused, but not against the private respondents
appeal_history: Trial court: Allowed application under Section 319 CrPC; High Court: Quashed and set aside the order; Supreme Court: Allowed appeals, restored the order of the Trial Court
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the trial court was justified in summoning the private respondents as additional accused based on the statement of the appellant, who was the injured eye witness, and that the High Court's quashing of the order was unsustainable in law and on facts.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court was justified in quashing the order passed by the trial court, as the statement of the appellant was not sufficient to invoke Section 319 CrPC, and that the High Court correctly observed that the appellant's account contained exaggerations and implications.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the power under Section 319 CrPC can be exercised even on the basis of the examination-in-chief of a witness, and that a prima facie case is sufficient to summon an additional accused, without requiring the evidence to be tested by cross-examination.
precedent_relied_upon: Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab (2014) 3 SCC 92; S. Mohammed Ispahani v. Yogendra Chandak (2017) 16 SCC 226; Sukhpal Singh Khaira v. State of Punjab (2019) 6 SCC 638; Rajesh v. State of Haryana (2019) 6 SCC 368
